subject: math
source: English National Curriculum — Mathematics programmes of study: key stages 1 and 2 (Year 3), DfE 2013

weeks.topic: Place value: hundreds, tens and ones
objectives: Recognise the place value of each digit in a 3-digit number
Represent numbers to 1,000 with base-10 and place-value charts

weeks.topic: Numbers to 1,000: read, write and find 10 or 100 more or less
objectives: Read and write numbers to 1,000 in numerals and words
Find 10 or 100 more or less than a given number

weeks.topic: Compare and order numbers to 1,000
objectives: Compare and order numbers up to 1,000 using <, > and =
Solve number problems involving place value

weeks.topic: Counting in 4s, 8s, 50s and 100s
objectives: Count from 0 in multiples of 4, 8, 50 and 100
Continue and explain number sequences

weeks.topic: Mental addition and subtraction with 3-digit numbers
objectives: Add and subtract mentally a 3-digit number and ones, tens or hundreds
Use known number bonds to 10 and 100

weeks.topic: Column addition with exchanging
objectives: Add numbers with up to three digits using the column method
Exchange ten ones for one ten when needed

weeks.topic: Column subtraction with exchanging
objectives: Subtract numbers with up to three digits using the column method
Exchange one ten for ten ones

weeks.topic: Estimating answers and checking with the inverse
objectives: Estimate the answer to a calculation
Use inverse operations to check answers

weeks.topic: Addition and subtraction word problems
objectives: Solve problems including missing-number problems
Choose an efficient mental or written method

weeks.topic: The 3 times table and fact families
objectives: Recall multiplication and division facts for the 3 times table
Link multiplication and division as inverses

weeks.topic: The 4 and 8 times tables
objectives: Recall multiplication and division facts for the 4 and 8 times tables
Use doubling to connect the 2, 4 and 8 times tables

weeks.topic: Mental multiplication: multiples of ten and 2-digit × 1-digit
objectives: Use known facts to multiply multiples of ten
Multiply 2-digit by 1-digit numbers by partitioning

weeks.topic: Written multiplication: 2-digit × 1-digit
objectives: Use arrays and the grid method to multiply
Move towards a formal written method

weeks.topic: Division with remainders and scaling problems
objectives: Divide 2-digit by 1-digit numbers using known facts
Solve scaling and correspondence problems

weeks.topic: Review: place value and the four operations
objectives: Revise column methods for addition and subtraction
Practise the 3, 4 and 8 times tables in mixed problems

weeks.topic: Money: pounds and pence, giving change
objectives: Add and subtract amounts of money in practical contexts
Give change using pounds and pence

weeks.topic: Statistics: pictograms, bar charts and tables
objectives: Interpret and present data using pictograms, bar charts and tables
Answer one-step and two-step questions about data

weeks.topic: Length: millimetres, centimetres and metres
objectives: Measure, compare, add and subtract lengths
Choose suitable units of length

weeks.topic: Perimeter of 2D shapes
objectives: Measure the perimeter of simple 2D shapes
Calculate perimeter by adding side lengths

weeks.topic: Fractions: unit and non-unit fractions
objectives: Recognise and write unit and non-unit fractions
Compare and order unit fractions

weeks.topic: Tenths: counting and dividing by 10
objectives: Count up and down in tenths
Recognise tenths that come from dividing an object or number by 10

weeks.topic: Fractions of a set of objects
objectives: Find unit and non-unit fractions of a set of objects
Use bar models to find fractions of amounts

weeks.topic: Equivalent fractions with small denominators
objectives: Recognise and show equivalent fractions using diagrams
Use a fraction wall to find equivalents

weeks.topic: Adding and subtracting fractions within one whole
objectives: Add and subtract fractions with the same denominator within one whole
Solve simple fraction problems

weeks.topic: Mass: kilograms and grams (Year 3)
objectives: Measure, compare, add and subtract mass
Read scales with different intervals

weeks.topic: Capacity and volume: litres and millilitres
objectives: Measure, compare, add and subtract volume and capacity
Read measuring jugs accurately

weeks.topic: Mid-year assessment: number, fractions and measures
objectives: Show clear methods in arithmetic and reasoning questions
Apply fractions and measures to problems

weeks.topic: Time: Roman numerals and analogue clocks
objectives: Tell the time on analogue clocks with Roman numerals I to XII
Tell the time to the nearest minute

weeks.topic: Time: 12-hour and 24-hour clocks, am and pm
objectives: Read time on 12-hour and 24-hour clocks
Use am, pm, morning, afternoon, noon and midnight

weeks.topic: Time: durations, seconds and the calendar
objectives: Compare durations of events in seconds, minutes and hours
Know the number of days in each month, year and leap year

weeks.topic: Angles as turns and right angles
objectives: Recognise angles as a property of shape or a description of a turn
Identify right angles, half turns and three-quarter turns

weeks.topic: Acute and obtuse angles
objectives: Identify whether angles are greater or smaller than a right angle
Classify angles as acute or obtuse

weeks.topic: Horizontal, vertical, parallel and perpendicular lines
objectives: Identify horizontal and vertical lines
Identify pairs of parallel and perpendicular lines

weeks.topic: 2D and 3D shapes: drawing and making
objectives: Draw 2D shapes and make 3D shapes using modelling materials
Describe faces, edges and vertices

weeks.topic: Mixed reasoning and problem solving
objectives: Solve multi-step problems from across the year
Explain thinking using mathematical vocabulary

weeks.topic: End-of-year assessment: Year 3 mathematics
objectives: Complete arithmetic and reasoning papers
Check answers using inverse operations and estimation

weeks.topic: Review and transition to Year 4
objectives: Reflect on strengths and targets for next year
Preview counting in 6s, 7s and 9s
